articles.title: Misery Index: Michigan's controversial win demands a deeper look and clearer answers
articles.summary: If we have to worry about someone from a conference office playing god with video replay to give a favored team one more chance to avoid an embarrassing upse...
articles.body:
We all celebrate the beginning of a new college football season because, no matter what kind of nonsense is happening off the field, we believe that once the competition begins it will unfold the way it always has.

That didn't happen in Ann Arbor, Michigan, on Saturday night. Not even close. Instead, the decision to give Michigan an extra second against Western Michigan — when the live video showed the clock expired and Bryce Underwood's Hail Mary pass still in the air — could turn into one of the biggest on-field scandals in college football history.

Welcome to another year of the Misery Index, a weekly feature where Yahoo Sports takes the temperature of college football fan bases that, as college football fan bases tend to do, react badly to losses, or sometimes even wins.

But unfortunately, the 2026 season must start with a story that should make all of us miserable.

Because if we can't trust the game to be over when the clock we see on television hits 0:00, if we have to hold our breath because we're afraid someone from a conference office is going to play god with video replay to give a favored team one more chance to avoid an embarrassing upset, then what's the point of playing the game in the first place?

Michigan was declared the winner, 13-12 , when Underwood's second Hail Mary connected. But anyone with honest eyes knows the Wolverines' win should be considered suspect, and the Big Ten's explanation two hours later was deeply unsatisfying.

The Big Ten says the clock on TV was not quite in sync with what was happening in the stadium and released a video that supposedly supports their position. But since the clock doesn't show fractions of a second and is only shown at the very end of the Big Ten's video rather than counting down from the start of the play, their explanation comes down to this: "Trust us, bro."

Maybe the Big Ten is right. MAC commissioner Jon Steinbrecher released a statement accepting what the Big Ten showed him , so perhaps that will be the end of it.

But football is the only sport where this is an issue. In basketball, for instance, you can see when the shot clock lights up red on the backboard and whether a player has or hasn't released a shot from their fingertips when that light turns on. Even if it's close, there's usually a definitive angle.

Nothing about this is definitive. And every player involved in trying to catch that ball was out of bounds, which makes it hard to explain why Michigan deserved to get that second back. Common sense tells you that when the clock hits 0:00 and the ball is still in the air, the game should be over.

If there's a big enough margin for error in how the clocks are synced to give Michigan one more play in that circumstance, that's a major trust issue for college football.

We need the Big Ten to do the honorable thing and launch a thorough, independent investigation into everyone involved in this decision. We deserve answers.

A multibillion dollar business should not be relying on the Big Ten replay booth to make a replay decision that swings a game to benefit a Big Ten team over a non-Big Ten team.

But this is about more than the result of one game. It's about the integrity of a sport that, as we've seen from the Brendan Sorsby controversy and the LSU mess , can rise up and demand fairness when it wants to.

Western Michigan has every right to feel cheated, and every person who watched that should have serious questions about why the call on the field got overturned under less-than-obvious circumstances.

The Big Ten will certainly hope that its statement Saturday is the end of it, but stories like this tend to take on a life of their own. The Big Ten better buckle up, because if we can't trust the clock, we can't trust anything. For Western Michigan and anyone who thinks the better team should win without a replay booth intervention, 2026 is off to a pretty miserable start.

ACC: In July, Dabo Swinney showed up at ACC media days and started reciting his résumé, which is what he always does when the questions get tough. It doesn't matter if it's the ink-stained wretches in the press room or Tyler from Spartanburg calling his radio show. At Clemson, you don't dare question King Dabo or suggest that he's lost the plot because you should be grateful for everything he's done. That's his version, at least. But given that we've all watched Clemson decline in real time during this decade, it felt extremely off-key for Swinney to come off a deeply embarrassing 7-6 season and once again start talking about the championships he won when college football had completely different rules than it does today. And when you aren't serious about fixing what's broken, you get what Clemson looks like now as a program: Soft, stale and irrelevant. Sure, it's no easy assignment to open the season at LSU. But Clemson was so uncompetitive in a 51-10 loss , Swinney has no choice anymore but to own this, to admit that he's let his program wither in the NIL era and to either get serious about changing their reality or retire. It's time for everyone at Clemson to stop treating this man with kid gloves and make him understand that nobody — even a two-time national championship coach — gets a lifetime pass.

Big Ten: The crazy part about Rutgers losing to UMass isn't just the 37-21 final score or how the Scarlet Knights were manhandled by a MAC team. Rutgers, according to multiple sources, actually paid a lot of money for this roster — far more than any Group of Six team and potentially in the $30 million range. And if that's not bad enough, an athletic department already swimming in red ink would owe Greg Schiano $18.5 million if they fired him after this year. All things considered, Rutgers may at this moment be the most hopeless situation in college football. Though it was sensible to bring Schiano back in 2020, he is 31-42 in his second stint. With the Big Ten getting so much better and Schiano getting so much older than he was 20 years ago when he turned Rutgers into a really good Big East program, it's just not going to work in its current form. Unless there's a massive and immediate turnaround, Rutgers athletic director Keli Zinn needs to start thinking about a new solution.

Big 12: Oklahoma State was so bad last season that almost anything would represent improvement. But after firing Mike Gundy and importing practically the entire North Texas program, including head coach Eric Morris and quarterback Drew Mestemaker, the Cowboys actually lost by a larger margin to Tulsa than they did last year. Morris' Oklahoma State debut, a 24-10 loss to their in-state rival , was probably more disheartening than the 19-12 loss that put Gundy on the hot seat. Think of it this way: If North Texas had played Tulsa last year in the American, they'd have been significant favorites. So why wouldn't the same personnel be able to deal with Tulsa now? It's strange, but it does illustrate the limits of trying to rebuild your program by taking someone else's. It doesn't mean Morris was a bad hire or that he shouldn't have brought over all those players from North Texas, but if you're an Oklahoma State fan it is a significant embarrassment to lose in consecutive years to a small, private, in-state school with a fraction of your budget. It also suggests the Cowboys have a long road to be as competitive as they were during Gundy's peak years.

SEC: Though the SEC did not lose a game Saturday, Auburn's 17-16 win over Baylor deserves a red flag. The main allure for hiring Alex Golesh is his offense — an up-tempo, spread-based offense that scored a ton of points at South Florida the last few years and at Tennessee before that. But the college football pendulum has swung back toward defense lately, and the main factor in Golesh becoming an attractive power conference candidate was South Florida outspending everyone else in the American Conference last season. It's too early to render a judgement on Golesh before he even coaches in an SEC game. But it was notable that Auburn's offense struggled quite a bit against Baylor, including quarterback Byrum Brown (a South Florida transfer) throwing three interceptions. Though Auburn's offense will certainly get sharper, will it be physical enough to compete in the SEC? For now, Tiger fans should be happy about the win. But they should be frightened about what's to come once conference play starts.

Group of Six: One of the biggest upsets in college football history happened on Sept. 5, 1992 when the Citadel beat Arkansas. The next day, Razorbacks coach Jack Crowe resigned. While the stakes were not nearly as high, it's kind of funny that the Citadel registered another FBS upset exactly 34 years later by beating Charlotte, 43-41. Keep in mind, the Citadel hasn't had a winning season since 2016 and went 4-8 last year. Tim Albin, the 49ers coach, went 33-19 in four seasons at Ohio. He's now 1-12 since moving to Charlotte, which might now be the worst program in FBS.

Brent Key: At any Georgia Tech game, you'll see a large number of fans wearing hats that say "Run The Damn Ball" in big letters. At a program that thrived for many years running Paul Johnson's triple option and has had a resurgence under Key, a former offensive line coach, being able to run the ball is not optional. So it should register as a huge concern that Georgia Tech managed just 51 yards on 30 carries while giving up three sacks in its 14-13 loss to Colorado . It was a bad night for Key on multiple fronts. Between failing to run the play clock all the way down late in the game when Georgia Tech had the lead, wasting a timeout on Colorado's game-winning drive when the Buffaloes were going to spike the ball, then playing for a 45-yard field goal to win instead of trying to get closer for kicker Aidan Birr (whose game-winner was blocked), it was a game management debacle. But none of that matters if Georgia Tech's offensive line can't win the line of scrimmage. Knowing how much pride Key takes in being physical up front, it should be a personal humiliation to see his offensive line play so poorly.

Kalani Sitake: Though BYU blew out Utah Tech in its opener, things are strange in Provo. Amid speculation about friction between Sitake and athletic director Brian Santiago — a fire that Sitake poured gasoline on with some passive-aggressive public comments about their relationship — the school announced Aug. 27 that the football coach would report to a university vice president rather than the AD. And this is all happening less than a year after Sitake decided to stay at BYU rather than take an offer from Penn State. If you read between the lines, it's reasonable to conclude that Sitake did not believe Santiago was delivering on promises made with regard to football funding. "I'm easy to get along with as long as you just take care of our football team and take care of the boys," he told reporters when asked prior to the announcement what their relationship was like. Obviously, this is an unsustainable situation — and not an internal fight that fans want to see spilling out into public view in a year when they should contend for the College Football Playoff.

Jamey Chadwell: Few schools in the country are getting less value for their money than Liberty. Though his contract is not public, Liberty lured Chadwell from Coastal Carolina with a contract believed to be worth around $4 million per year. That means Chadwell is being paid like a low-end power conference coach while delivering alarmingly bad results for multiple years in a row. In fact, going back to the 2024 season, Liberty has won just seven of its last 20 games, including Saturday's 20-13 loss to James Madison. And this is happening while the school continues to pour resources into the program and, at least on paper, has landed highly ranked high school and transfer classes. One major source of frustration for Liberty fans is committing 12 penalties for 82 yards Saturday, continuing a trend of sloppy play from recent seasons. Given its willingness to spend money, Liberty should be dominating C-USA. If they don't, it's squarely on Chadwell.

Sonny Dykes: We are a week late acknowledging the disaster that is TCU, but timing should not protect those who deserve a good Misery Index lashing. And the moment TCU decided to suspend the media credentials of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram for committing an act of journalism, we should have known that karma was headed their way. The local newspaper did its job, reporting on a locker room fight that left receiver Dozie Ezukanma with serious injuries requiring hospitalization. The school decided to punish the messenger and then subsequently lost its season opener to North Carolina, 15-10. Though TCU reversed its decision and restored access for the only media outlet that covers the program on a daily basis, it's a classic case of worrying about the wrong things. If Dykes lands on the hot seat this season — a distinct possibility if they're really as bad as they looked against the Tar Heels — it would be a shocking fall for a coach who had his team playing in the national title game just four years ago. But he wouldn't get a lot of sympathy from those who prefer the truth coming to light.

Enough, Kirk Herbstreit: America has been very kind to Herbstreit as he's turned his dogs into ESPN celebrities. But opening a pop-up store this weekend in Baton Rouge to sell merchandise with the image of his golden retriever, Peter, is the kind of self-indulgence that needs to be addressed. Herbie, with all due respect, it's gone too far and we're now at the point where people are unafraid to call it out. Dogs are wonderful creatures, and it is terrific that you find comfort in their companionship. But your relationship with them is not unique or special. A lot of people have dogs, a lot of people love dogs, and a lot of people need dogs for physical and emotional support. Pushing it to the point where you're selling dog merch and shoving it down everyone's throat at every opportunity is, frankly, a little weird.

Josh Hoover had a bloody face: There is perhaps something cool about playing football with blood streaming down your face and all over your uniform, but it was a little too reminiscent of Hannibal Lecter having a friend for dinner to see Hoover stay in the game against North Texas on Saturday after a violent facemask penalty. It wasn't his fault, and we should give Hoover props for toughness. But it's also very gross.

Ryan Coleman-Williams continues to drop passes: Though Alabama had no problems in a 48-10 win over East Carolina, the Crimson Tide's star receiver is still having issues catching the football. A year ago, Coleman-Williams led the FBS in dropped passes. He started 2026 with a couple more that were pretty egregious. Williams has decided not to wear gloves this season, but maybe he should reassess because it didn't seem to help in Week 1.

articles.title: FIFA’s Infantino avoids questions on his future amid growing uncertainty
articles.summary: Upon arrival at the U-20 Women’s World Cup, Infantino remained tight-lipped about his re-election as FIFA president.
articles.body:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino is staying mum on the leadership challenge he faces as a result of his failed plan to sell rights to private investors in the World Cup, and he declined to answer questions about his re-election upon arrival at the Under-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland.

Infantino, who faces continuing pressure and the prospect of a criminal case, was in the stands speaking with Polish football federation president Cezary Kulesza as hosts Poland faced Argentina on the opening day of the tournament on Saturday.

However, when he arrived at the Arena Katowice, the 56-year-old avoided questions about his future at the global governing body for football.

“There will be a lot to say, but there will be a right place and a right time to say this. It’s not today, it’s not here, but here and today, we are enjoying football,” Infantino told British broadcaster Sky News outside the venue.

“We are continuing at FIFA, of course, to work to give every corner of the world a chance, an opportunity, a dignity, to find ways and means for them to become better and to participate and to celebrate football, which we all love.”

Infantino did not answer when asked if he had considered resigning or whether he still intends to stand for a fourth term next year.

Infantino had mostly kept out of the spotlight in the weeks since his World Cup sell-off plan fell apart amid opposition from many FIFA member nations and some of his own officials.

The European nations — a quarter of the 24-team field — backed down on a boycott threat last week, citing assurances from FIFA that the plan would not be revived.

Legal action over the original attempt continues, and Europe has a leading role in efforts to oust Infantino ahead of next year’s FIFA election.

A court filing by FIFA on Thursday accused UEFA of running a “smear campaign against FIFA and its leadership” as the European football body seeks discovery of evidence related to the FIFA Forward Enterprise plan.

Infantino infuriated football leaders worldwide in July, shortly after the World Cup ended, when his plan for a $20bn subsidiary controlling FIFA commercial rights, including the World Cup, was revealed by British daily The Times.

The spinoff was to be 20 percent owned by investors led by a New York fund created by Joshua Kushner, whose initial money was to pay offers of $20m to each of FIFA’s 211 member federations. They were given a mid-September deadline to accept.

The FIFA president dropped his proposal within four days. UEFA had support from the Asian Football Confederation and North American football body CONCACAF, and there was criticism of the plan and of Infantino from senior FIFA officials.

articles.title: Un David Otorbi distinto al del 17 de agosto de 2024 ante el Barcelona
articles.standfirst: El extremo de la cantera emerge en este momento de crisis tras dos años en el olvido... cuando debutó en Liga por sorpresa ante el Barça en la primera jornada y desapareció
articles.summary: El extremo de la cantera emerge en este momento de crisis tras dos años en el olvido... cuando debutó en Liga por sorpresa ante el Barça en la primera jornada y desapareció
articles.body: Han transcurrido dos años del debut de David Otorbi como jugador del Valencia en un partido de Liga. Aquella calurosa noche del 17 de agosto de 2024 era su primer partido de Liga. Todo un Valencia-Barcelona para abrir el telón liguero y de repente, emergió la figura del canterano. Rubén Baraja, que por entonces ejercía de entrenador del Valencia, dio entrada al extremo en un partido top de la Liga. Casi que fue por sorpresa -jugó el último cuarto de hora de aquel encuentro-, ya que no volvió a tener minutos jamás... hasta este año en la Liga. Su debut liguero oficial se produjo ese día de agosto, ingresando al terreno de juego desde el banquillo a la edad de 16 años y 306 días. Con este hito, superó el récord anterior de precocidad liguera en el club de Mestalla. Pero fue fugaz. Ya no contó para Baraja en Liga ni para Corberán en año y medio -sólo en dos partidos de Copa ante Maracena y Sporting- pese a que desde la campaña pasada había sido habitual en convocatorias. Lo que sucede es que ahora el equipo anda corto de jugadores de banda. De extremos. Y el entrenador de Cheste tuvo que verse obligado a echar mano de Otorbi en el duelo ante el Betis. 'Redebutó' dos años después en partido de Liga. Apenas tres o cuatro minutos, pero dejó tan buenas prestaciones por su profundidad -concepto que echa en falta este equipo en este arranque de competición- que ha sido poco de lo positivo hasta el momento. Gracias a esos minutos volvió a contar con otra oportunidad en Riazor ante el Dépor. Esta vez con más tiempo sobre el césped. Concretamente media hora. Y ahora llega el Barcelona en Mestalla con este gran recuerdo para el canterano. Porque si sigue la tendencia que hay, va a seguir contando con minutos y tiene la oportunidad de medirse de nuevo al Barcelona en Mestalla. Dos años después. Con un Otorbi distinto. Con dos años más de experiencia, con mucho banquillo escuchando consejos y tratando de aprender... A todo ello, David Otorbi ya ostentaba previamente el récord absoluto como el debutante más joven del club en cualquier competición oficial, tras haber jugado meses antes (el 7 de enero de 2024) en un encuentro de la Copa del Rey contra el Cartagena en el estadio de Cartagonova. Lo hizo con tan solo 16 años, 2 meses y 19 días. Superó a Diego Ribera que tenía la marca desde 1994.

articles.title: Brotes verdes con Julián Alvarez
articles.standfirst: Gustó su actitud en la media hora que tuvo tras su polémico culebrón. “Le tenemos que recuperar”, insisten en el Atlético
articles.summary: Gustó su actitud en la media hora que tuvo tras su polémico culebrón. “Le tenemos que recuperar”, insisten en el Atlético
articles.body: “Le tenemos que recuperar”, es la frase más repetida en en el Atlético en las últimas semanas. Hablamos, claro, de Julián y del sentimiento dentro del vestuario una vez pasada la tormenta desatada por el propio delantero… en connivencia con su entorno y un Barcelona donde los rojiblancos insisten por pasiva y activa que no jugará. “Todos sabemos lo que puede dar”, afirmaba Barrios todavía en las entrañas de San Mamés. El palo que supuso el 3-0 mostraba un único brote verde. Y es que los 30 minutos que saltó al campo Julián dejaron una versión diametralmente opuesta a la del partido del Villarreal, donde la Araña deambuló por el verde sin aportar nada más allá. Tocó fondo y era la hora, insisten en los despachos, de recuperarlo. Pero la sensación dentro del club y la caseta es que el fin del mercado ha empezado a resetear la cabeza del 19. Lo ha pasado muy mal, como reconoció el propio Gil Marín, pero ahora va centrando poco a poco el tiro en recuperar su mejor versión como demostró en su entrada en San Mamés. Fue el mejor de los cuatro que salieron a la vez para dar la vuelta al 2-0, protagonizando la ocasión más clara y buscando el esférico sin cesar. La actitud, así las cosas, viró como lleva días haciéndolo también en los entrenamientos. Siempre arropado por Musso, Giuliano y el Cuti, no dudó en ir a aplaudir a los 200 hinchas desplazados a Bilbao. Cierto que su cara está alejada todavía de esa felicidad que mostró en su primera temporada, pero también que nada tiene que ver con lo vivido en su anterior partido… y en ese viaje a ningún lado que fue su deseo de marcharse al Barcelona. La de San Mamés fue una prueba de fuego, claro. Pero vienen más y de qué nivel. La primera, la visita a un Anfield que conoce a la perfección. Y el estreno en una Champions que ya ha ganado y que el curso pasado fue la única competición donde mostró lo mejor de sí. A Julián le motiva la orejona y sus 10 tantos en la pasada edición son el mejor ejemplo de ello. No hay que olvidar que la final de este año se disputa en el Metropolitano, estadio en el que Julián pasó su peor momento ante el Villarreal pero coliseo que sabe que no hay otro talento mayor en la plantilla que un Alvarez que tiene que convertir estos brotes verdes en algo cotidiano para lograr reconducir su situación en el Atlético.

articles.title: Scott Bain: Is Falkirk goalkeeper on course to be Scotland's number one?
articles.summary: With Sebastien Pocognoli looking to change the way Scotland play, might Scott Bain be the answer to his goalkeeping problems?
articles.body:
Eight saves, many of them excellent. Good distribution. And a man of the match performance. If timing is everything, Falkirk goalkeeper Scott Bain may just have played his way into the forefront of the new Scotland head coach's thinking.

Sebastien Pocognoli will soon be announcing his first squad for the forthcoming Nations League games.

With the retirement of Craig Gordon and the lack of recent first-team minutes for Angus Gunn and Liam Kelly - the other two World Cup squad goalkeepers - is Bain the obvious answer to Pocognoli's potential problem?

On the evidence of his display in the 1-1 draw against Dundee United on Saturday - without which his side may well have been beaten given the number of chances United created - he'll be very unlucky not to be recalled to the international fold.

Unsurprisingly, Bain's manager John McGlynn was happy to sing his praises.

"I thought he was terrific," McGlynn said of the 34-year-old, who has earned four caps over the past eight years.

"If you're looking for a goalkeeper who can play from the back and still make saves and bring composure and calmness to your defence, then I think Scott ticks all the boxes. So I have no doubt that the manager will be looking at him."

Stoppage-time concession denies Falkirk first win

Latest Falkirk news, analysis and fan views

There will be a number of Dundee United players cursing Bain's name after Saturday's game.

Full-back Kevin Ciubotaru's shot seemed destined for the bottom right-hand corner before Bain intervened. United debutant Lyall Cameron also watched in anguish as Bain denied him.

Another new boy, Zidane Iqbal, arrowed a shot towards the top corner only for Bain to tip it away. And the goalkeeper thwarted Neil Farrugia, too.

It was a heroic display of defiance that very nearly earned his side a first league win of the season, but for Michael Forbes' stoppage-time header.

After a mistake at Celtic Park last weekend, Bain was back to his best.

United assistant manager Lee Sharp was also quick to praise Bain's contribution and agree that he's done his Scotland chances absolutely no harm whatsoever.

"Absolutely," he said. "He had two or three really good saves in the second half."

That was perhaps an understatement. Falkirk faced 27 shots, nine of which were on target. All of which were repelled by Bain until the late leveller.

He has now played 44 games for Falkirk, keeping 10 clean sheets in the process. He kept the ball out of the net in half of his 78 games for Celtic prior to that.

At Dundee, Bain's stats were pretty good, too - 21 clean sheets in 124 games.

Alex McLeish gave him his Scotland debut against Mexico in June 2018, after which he played a further three times for his country. His last cap came against Ivory Coast in a pre-World Cup friendly in March but he did not make the finals squad.

On his current form, he'll have every right to hope there's a new lease of international life coming in Pocognoli's brave new vision for Scotland.

articles.title: Alemania ya conoce la magia de Chuki
articles.standfirst: El media punta pucelano firmó ante el Leipzig su primer pase de gol de la temporada y brilló en el triunfo del Werder Bremen
articles.summary: El media punta pucelano firmó ante el Leipzig su primer pase de gol de la temporada y brilló en el triunfo del Werder Bremen
articles.body: El Werder apostó por Chuki para marcar la diferencia y el atacante está empezando a demostrarlo. El joven media punta —generación 2004— dejó ante el RB Leipzig su primer gran partido ante su nueva afición. En un choque de máxima exigencia, frente a uno de los gallos de la Bundesliga, apareció cuando su equipo más lo necesitaba y dejó varias acciones de talento, ese talento único con el que se abrió camino en el Real Valladolid. La asistencia del primer gol de los verdes fue una delicia, en fondo y forma. El Werder se activó para recuperar tras un saque de banda del Leipzig e hizo llegar con éxito el balón a la frontal, para Chuki, que en pleno despliegue giro y a la primera, filtró el balón y dibujó con un magnífico pase al espacio para la llegada de Dinkçi, que rompió desde la derecha para poner el 1-0. Pura electricidad, un toque decisivo, puro Chuki. Una acción de auténtico ’10’. El entrenador Daniel Thioune le está dando libertad total por detrás de Niclas Füllkrug (ídolo que ha vuelto tras rodar por Dortmund, Milan y West Ham), y las empiezas están encajando, con Marco Grüll a la izquierda y el doble pivote neerlandés Ludovit Reis - Youri Regeer. No fue su única aparición. En la segunda parte estuvo muy cerca de marcar después de recoger un balón suelto en la frontal del área. Su disparo se marchó rozando el palo izquierdo de Vandevoordt, portero del Red Bull. Hubiera sido un golazo, muy Chuki, por esa capacidad del pucelano de transformar un balón ’normal’ en una acción de peligro. Y cuando el partido entraba en su tramo decisivo, volvió a aparecer: una pelota al área —llevaba veneno— terminó provocando el 3-0. El Weserstadion ya sabe quién es Iván San José Cantalejo. El público despidió al pucelano con una gran ovación. Chuki (22 años) llegó al Werder Bremen procedente del Valladolid a finales de la pasada temporada, después de finalizar su contrato. Desde el primer momento fue recibido como una de las grandes apuestas de futuro del club y uno de los nombres que más ilusión generaba dentro del proyecto 2026-27. El verano ha servido para adaptarse a un nuevo fútbol, a un nuevo país, a un nuevo idioma y a una competición de máxima exigencia. La temporada pasada firmó siete goles y ocho asistencias, fundamentales para entender la permanencia del Pucela en Segunda. Nunca había jugado lejos de casa. Poco a poco, empieza a despegar. Ya tuvo minutos en Copa, fue titular en la dolorosa derrota ante el Friburgo y ayer, en el primer partido de la temporada en casa, dio un paso adelante. Y lo hizo de la mejor manera posible: siendo decisivo. El Werder ha construido un equipo con una mezcla de experiencia y juventud. En ese proyecto, Chuki aparece como uno de los talentos a seguir. No es casualidad que su llegada generase tanta expectación: el club sabía que incorporaba a un futbolista con personalidad, ambición y un techo alto, por descubrir. Uno de los objetivos del futbolista siempre ha sido tener una oportunidad en la selección española Sub-21 y consolidarse dentro de un bloque que tiene Eurocopa de la categoría el próximo verano, que repartirá plazas para los Juegos Olímpicos. En los últimos años, varios futbolistas españoles han dado el salto a la Bundesliga con diferentes recorridos y trayectorias. Chuki quiere escribir el suyo.

articles.title: Sancet brilla con el balón y el corazón
articles.standfirst: Coronó con un gol de dedicatoria muy especial su excelente partido ante el Atlético
articles.summary: Coronó con un gol de dedicatoria muy especial su excelente partido ante el Atlético
articles.body: Domingo y lunes serán días de descanso para un Athletic que enlaza dos victorias seguidas manteniendo su portería inmaculada. El Athletic de Terzic, que ha insistido en que no es su Athletic y sí el Athletic de todos además de reconocer el buen trabajo defensivo que se hizo también con Valverde antes de la última temporada, ha recuperado para la causa a Sancet. Oihan está dulce. El técnico pronosticó el viernes que pronto marcaría y el navarro lo hizo al día siguiente para poner la última firma al triunfo ante el Atlético. Sancet brilló con el balón y el corazón. Celebró con ganas el tanto y nada más marcar hizo una X con sus manos. El gesto provocó un escalofrío de emoción entre los que conocían el motivo. Lo cuenta Alberto Santacruz (RADIO MARCA BILBAO), conocedor del motivo. “La X es por Xanet, el chico del Iturrigorri que con sólo 9 años murió en abril víctima de un accidente de tráfico. Paule, la hermana de Xanet, estuvo en la UCI y Sancet estuvo visitándola. Desde que se enteró del accidente ha estado muy cercano a la familia, que un día les dijo que le dedicase un gol”, explicó. La reacción de Sancet no la esperaban porque tampoco conocían que la dedicatoria sería pública ni en qué consistiría. “Le están muy agradecidos. La familia se ha pegado una llorera importante por la emoción del momento y el buen gesto de Sancet”, añade. El futbolista no trató el asunto después en la sala de prensa, pues no se considera protagonista de nada y sólo quería ofrecer cariño con un emotivo recuerdo.. El mediapunta recibió elogios de Terzic por su buena disposición durante el encuentro. “Ha jugado en varias posiciones. Va a ser muy importante y puede ser uno de los mejores de la Liga”. El futbolista recogió el reto. “Nos sentimos muy identificados con lo que nos pide el míster. Sé que tengo potencial y estoy en seguir trabajando para dar lo mejor de mí”, señaló.

articles.title: Uriarte tercia: deja las invitaciones a la plantilla y se las corta al resto de colectivos implicados
articles.standfirst: El presidente aplaza su plan final hasta que se produzca la conversación con los capitanes
articles.summary: El presidente aplaza su plan final hasta que se produzca la conversación con los capitanes
articles.body: el recorte de invitaciones y pases de favor en San Mamés es una de las medidas implementadas por Jon Uriarte en este arranque de temporada. Y el presidente ha mantenido su plan con todos los colectivos afectados....salvo con la plantilla. Los futbolistas del primer equipo del Athletic fueron advertidos de que no contarían con entradas gratis en el partido ante el Atlético, pero tras su protesta en solidaridad con afectados por otros problemas internos y pedir una reunión con el presidente éste decidió aplazar la retirada de las mismas. Todos los jugadores tuvieron entradas frente al Atlético. La reunión lleva más de diez días esperando para celebrarse y se espera que pueda darse esta semana. Los futbolistas del Athletic protestaron con dureza por muchas de las medidas ejecutadas por la Junta Directiva "que se han hecho bola en estos cuatro años". Pusieron a Uriarte en una difícil situación, pero el presidente lo ha manejado con extrema sangre fría. Los jugadores no han vuelto a protestar y el presidente, que no se ha reunido todavía con ellos, abrió la mano a las invitaciones ante el Atlético cuando no lo hizo con el resto de colectivos afectados. Así, no las tuvieron los expresidentes, ni los trabajadores del club ni los exfutbolistas. Tampoco hubo entradas de más para el Atlético, al que se cumplimentó con el mínimo exigido en el convenio con Liga y RFEF. Los expresidentes recibieron el jueves la propuesta de un asiento vitalicio en el palco -antes tenían la posibilidad de invitaciones en Tribuna Sur Alta- pero ninguno hizo uso del mismo y siguieron el encuentro desde sus respectivas localidades. Empleados del club, que habían enviado una carta a la entidad, y exjugadores no recibieron ninguna. La Asociación de Veteranos está molesta por el trato y la situación en la que quedan para muchos aficionados porque da la sensación de que sólo piden y reciben cuando ellos participan en múltiples actividades de representación de la entidad sin nada a cambio. Casualidad o no, ningún exfutbolista del club ha participado como comentarista en los partidos que han seguido al de la protesta de la primera plantilla ante el Barcelona. La crisis de las invitaciones esconde otros problemas internos de la entidad que estas últimas campañas implican a empleados y también a futbolistas y técnicos de las categorías inferiores del club con los que en el primer equipo se han querido solidarizar. Que el primer equipo haya contado con invitaciones no modifica la necesidad de una reunión con el presidente porque los capitanes quieren transmitir todas esas circunstancias. Y los futbolistas también saben que su posición sería más que delicada ante aficionados y distintos sectores de la entidad de enfríar ahora su posición sólo por disponer de entradas.

articles.title: El difícil aterrizaje de Arbeloa: primeros abucheos y un 0 de 9 que amenaza con ampliarse
articles.standfirst: La derrota ante el Palace provocó las primeras críticas de parte de la afición de Craven Cottage
articles.summary: La derrota ante el Palace provocó las primeras críticas de parte de la afición de Craven Cottage
articles.body: Tres partidos en Premier y tres derrotas. La aventura de Álvaro Arbeloa en Inglaterra no ha empezado como el técnico soñaba. Más allá de su victoria en Copa de la Liga (ante el Wimbledon de League One), el Fulham cuenta sus partidos por derrotas en la competición doméstica. Sigue a cero, con siete tantos encajados en tres partidos, aunque no es colista por su mejor diferencia de goles respecto al Coventry. Ese 0 de 9 ha traído los primeros nervios en Craven Cottage. De hecho, Arbeloa y sus jugadores escucharon abucheos de una parte de sus aficionados tras la dolorosa derrota de este sábado ante el Crystal Palace. El Fulham, pese a adelantarse por dos veces en el marcador, acabó cayendo por 2-3 ante un rival que anotó tres dianas en cinco disparos a puerta. Baste señalar la diferencia de goles esperados: 3,13 del Fulham por 1,97 del Palace. Al igual que en los partidos anteriores, esas mejores estadísticas no tuvieron reflejo en el marcador final. Precisamente, a esa falta de pegada se agarró Arbeloa para explicar un traspié con el que no contaba: "Perdimos un partido que no merecíamos perder. Fuimos el mejor equipo en el campo, pero al final, en el fútbol, hay que aprovechar las oportunidades y ellos lo hicieron mejor que nosotros. Recibimos goles muy fáciles. El Crystal Palace no necesitó hacer mucho para marcar tres goles. Nosotros tenemos que hacer muchas cosas si queremos marcar un gol". Tampoco invita al optimismo el calendario inmediato del Fulham previo al parón de selecciones. A Arbeloa y los suyos les toca visitar al Liverpool de Iraola antes de disputar en casa la tercera ronda de la Copa de la Liga contra el West Ham y enfrentarse al Manchester United en Premier. El técnico, no obstante, prefiere ver el vaso medio lleno ante la dificultad: "Son tres partidos y tres derrotas. Y ahora piensas que tenemos que ir a Anfield, el United viene a Craven Cottage. Se avecinan dos partidos muy difíciles y, además, en la Carabao tenemos que enfrentarnos al West Ham United, así que, evidentemente, no será fácil”. Pese a los malos resultados iniciales, nadie en el Fulham cuestiona la figura de Álvaro Arbeloa. Al menos, de momento. El técnico firmó en julio un contrato de tres años y el club se ha gastado este verano más de 100 millones de libras en siete fichajes para su nuevo proyecto. De sus palabras, se deduce la confianza que siente el técnico de los propietarios: "Sabíamos que este mes iba a ser muy duro, pero les dije a mis jugadores que este mes no definirá toda nuestra temporada. Creo que están trabajando muy duro. Con esta mentalidad y con este carácter, estoy seguro de que las victorias llegarán. Para los jugadores es una situación difícil, un momento difícil, pero estoy muy orgulloso de ellos”.

articles.summary: Los azulones afrontan desde el lunes hasta el 20 de septiembre cuatro jornadas ligueras

articles.title: Alerta roja para Anfield
articles.standfirst: Los problemas de Grimaldo para cerrar su banda avivan las dudas sin resolver en el lateral izquierdo de cursos anteriores. Galán ya padeció al Liverpool en dos minutos hace un año
articles.summary: Los problemas de Grimaldo para cerrar su banda avivan las dudas sin resolver en el lateral izquierdo de cursos anteriores. Galán ya padeció al Liverpool en dos minutos hace un año
articles.body: Sería tan alejado de la realidad personalizar en Grimaldo la derrota del Atlético en San Mamés como negar que Simeone sigue teniendo los mismos problemas en el lateral izquierdo que en años anteriores. Más aún en vísperas de visitar Anfield, donde hace un año Galán sufrió un martirio con Salah traducido en dos goles entre los minutos 4 y 6, el mismo tiempo que duró la desconexión rojiblanca en Bilbao en la que el internacional español apareció en la foto como uno de los peor parados. Así las cosas, la alerta roja para Liverpool ya está activada. Pese a que Grimaldo llegó al Metropolitano con la estrella de campeón del mundo en el pecho (por más que viera desde el banquillo cómo le dejaba sin minutos Cucurella, el gran objetivo que acarició el Atlético hasta que la irrupción del Real Madrid le obligó a pasar al plan B) y con unos números de 'delantero' tras su periplo por el Bayer Leverkusen (30 goles y 45 asistencias en 145 apariciones), sus primeros partidos como rojiblanco siembran las dudas sobre su rendimiento defensivo. Así, más allá del roto con el que Robert Navarro le dejó sentado en el área antes de firmar el 2-0 en San Mamés y de su 'ausencia' en su zona en el 1-0 en el que Hancko tuvo que acudir a tapar a Iñaki Williams, Grimaldo ya había dejado maniobrar a Miguel Sierra en el gol del Sevilla de la jornada anterior. Señales inequívocas de que El Cholo tiene trabajo por delante para poner fin a un problema que viene de lejos. Concretamente, desde que Filipe Luis y Lucas Hernández dejaron el Atlético en 2019, pues ninguno de sus sucesores llegarían a cubrir su vacío. A Lodi (por más que ganara la última Liga), Galán o Ruggeri (aunque llegara a salir indemne en algunos duelos con Lamine Yamal) les condenaron sus carencias defensivas, mientras que a Reinildo, un muro insuperable, le penalizaban sus dificultades para contribuir en la faceta ofensiva. De hecho, con Reguilón completando la nómina de laterales izquierdos que ahondaron en el agujero, no fueron pocas las ocasiones en las que los parches de Simeone acabaron siendo la solución, ya fuera reconvertir a Saúl, desplazar a Hermoso a la banda o apostar por un carrilero como Carrasco. Planes de emergencia que vuelven a vislumbrarse como posibilidad de cara a Anfield. Con este panorama, ya cobra fuerza la posibilidad de que Hancko sea el lateral izquierdo en Liverpool. Por un lado, para alicatar un flanco por el que pueden aparecer Víctor Muñoz o Barcola; por el otro, porque el Cuti Romero ya asoma como el líder que devuelva de una vez por todas a la defensa la solidez de antaño, la de los tiempos en los que Filipe o Lucas eran garantías en su banda. Cierto es que no es la posición natural del eslovaco, pero a falta de un especialista (por ahí se explica que se negociara hasta el último día de mercado con Tagliafico tratando de que cuadraran los números), se antoja como la mejor vía para recuperar el orden.

articles.title: From League One scare to Premier League heights
articles.summary: As recently as last year Hull avoided relegation to League One only on goal difference.  Fast-forward 16 months and they are now going toe to toe with the bi...
articles.body:
As recently as last year Hull avoided relegation to League One only on goal difference.

Fast-forward 16 months and they are now going toe to toe with the big names of the Premier League.

The turnaround can be traced back to the arrival of Sergej Jakirovic before last season.

The former Bosnia international joined a club under a transfer embargo, confining them to free transfers and loans, but still made them promotion contenders.

Jakirovic guided Hull to a play-off win against a Millwall side who finished three places and 10 points above them, before Oli McBurnie's last-gasp winner against Middlesbrough secured top-flight football.

And Hull did not stay still in the summer.

They were the busiest Premier League side with 18 new signings for about £150m, with six of them, including £22m midfielder Tim Iroegbunam from Everton , arriving on deadline day.

"I know the core of my team. This is the Championship players," said Jakirovic, who signed a two-year contract extension on Friday.

"We brought the players in to put some quality there.

"The big problem for me is who didn't have a pre-season. This is a very big problem. But we will try.

"For example, on Tuesday [against Sunderland in the Carabao Cup], we will use that to give minutes, and at the end they will get a new chance."

articles.title: “Belongs on a W Roster”: Turkey Star’s FIBA World Cup History Draws Strong Appeal From Veteran ESPN Studio Host
articles.summary: Turkish guard Sevgi Uzun set a record on the very first day of the 2026 FIBA World Cup, and her performance has drawn a bid for her to be in the world’s larg...
articles.body:
Turkish guard Sevgi Uzun set a record on the very first day of the 2026 FIBA World Cup, and her performance has drawn a bid for her to be in the world's largest women's basketball league, the WNBA. During the FIBA World Cup game between Belgium and Turkey, Uzun's record-setting play has drawn attention from all over the basketball world, and for one analyst, it signals a move to bigger things for the guard.

While Turkey went down 75-89 on September 4, guard Sevgi Uzun had a game for the ages. She finished the game with 11 points, four rebounds, and 11 assists with zero turnovers in 33 minutes, becoming the second player to log double-digit assists in a game this tournament. It drew the attention of ESPN studio host Cindy Brunson, who posted her reaction on X .

"[Uzun] belongs on a W roster," she wrote. "Just proves that it's hard to find a spot in the best league in the world & find a good fit for one's skill set too. #WNBA #FIBAWWC."

When asked about the potential for where she could play, Brunson was clear: expansion teams.

"More WNBA teams are on the way! Cleveland, Detroit & Philly (2028, 2029 & 2030)," she wrote. "The Cleveland Sirens rollout was top tier!"

Expansion teams, which will look for new players to cement a competitive roster, could be a great fit for an efficient guard with international experience like Uzun. With her posting double-digit assists, she joined USA guard Caitlin Clark as the player with the most assists in a World Cup debut and became the second player to drop 10 or more assists without turning the ball over a single time, following Clark. Clark did so against China on the same day as Uzun's game.

With her record, the 28-year-old Uzun has become the eighth player to record 11 or more assists in a single game, joining the elite company of Julie Allemand, Dawn Staley, and Yuka Harada alongside Clark.

Notably, the international stage is not an unfamiliar one for Uzun. The 28-year-old has been a part of Turkey's senior national team since 2018 and has been on this stage before. She has represented the country in EuroBasket in 2021, 2023, and 2025, and has shown major improvement with each iteration of the tournament.

In the 2025 edition of EuroBasket, she averaged 13.7 points on 44.4% from the field and 40% from long range, along with 4.2 assists on 2.2 turnovers. Her skill set is easily translatable: a capable playmaker who can stretch the floor to open lanes for stars to operate inside the arc. In her most recent international matchup against Belgium in the 2026 FIBA World Cup, she was the second-highest scorer on the Turkish side, behind Kennedy Burke, who also plays for the Connecticut Sun as a guard.

However, Uzun isn't fighting to make the WNBA for the first time; she's trying to cement her spot in the league.

Why Sevgi Uzun Has Yet to Find Her WNBA Fit

Despite her solid international and club career in Europe, Sevgi Uzun has struggled to establish herself in the WNBA.

She signed with Dallas in 2024 as an undrafted free agent, playing all 40 games and averaging over 20 minutes per night. However, her efficiency was rough, since she ended up averaging just 4.4 points on 34.2% from the field and 23.8% from three.

Then, in the following offseason, she was traded to the Phoenix Mercury as part of a four-team trade that sent Satou Sabally and Alyssa Thomas to the Mercury. She played 25 games for the Mercury, with her efficiency getting even worse and her minutes reduced as a result.

She was traded midseason to the Chicago Sky, finishing the season averaging 3.1 points per game on 32.6% from the field. Lastly, ahead of the 2026 season, after she was waived by the Sky, she signed a training camp contract with the Los Angeles Sparks, but didn't end up making the final roster.

"We're looking forward to having Sev here in Los Angeles," then-Sparks General Manager Raegan Pebley said in a press release on April 18. "She's had a great season with [Fenerbahce], and we are eager to experience her impact on our organization."

Across her 65 games in the WNBA over 2 seasons, Uzun has averaged 3.9 points, but shoots from the field with 33.7% accuracy. As her 2.8 prove, Uzun's playmaking has never been in question. What she needs to do is improve her offensive efficiency, especially from three. If she can consistently space the floor, there's no doubt teams would pursue her for a bench spot, if not more.

What breaking the record does for Uzun is put more eyes on her, something that can help generate the buzz needed for WNBA GMs to take notice. Brunson's comments do just that.

articles.title: Is Lamine Yamal Playing Today for Valencia vs. Barcelona?
articles.summary: Valencia hosts Barcelona this Sunday, Sept. 6, on Matchday 4 of the 2026-27 La Liga season. Hansi Flick’s side currently sits atop the table with nine points...
articles.body:
Valencia hosts Barcelona this Sunday, Sept. 6, on Matchday 4 of the 2026-27 La Liga season. Hansi Flick's side currently sits atop the table with nine points after a perfect start of three games and three wins.

Their closest challenger is Real Madrid, also with nine points, but Barcelona has played one fewer game, so a victory over the Mestalla side would make them the outright leaders.

Ahead of this match, all eyes are on the team's star, Lamine Yamal. As is customary on every matchday, fans are wondering whether Yamal will play.

The answer is clear: yes, and here are the details.

Lamine Yamal's Two Goals in Last Match Boost Barcelona

Yamal is included in Barcelona's squad for this away match. Joining him are other forwards such as new signing Gabriel Jesus, Raphinha, Karim Adeyemi and Anthony Gordon .

With the talented Spanish winger available and fit, he is highly likely to start this match. Yamal has already scored two goals in Barcelona's first three La Liga matches this season, pointing to what could be a great campaign for the World Cup champion.

Those two goals in three matches came in just one game, the most recent one against Rayo Vallecano, which Barcelona won 5-2. In the 21st minute of that match, Yamal took advantage of a ball received from Marc Bernal and fired into the top right corner.

Later that same night, in the 90th minute, Yamal once again capitalized on an opportunity, this time assisted by his new teammate Adeyemi, and fired a precise shot into the bottom left corner.

With this excellent run of form, Yamal will therefore approach the match against Valencia highly motivated to become the outright leader of La Liga ahead of their biggest rivals, Real Madrid.

What's Next for Lamine Yamal & Barcelona

After their visit to Mestalla, Barcelona and Yamal will have to switch into UEFA Champions League mode, as their journey in Europe's top competition begins next Wednesday, Sept. 9.

On that day, the Catalan side will host Eredivisie side Feyenoord at Camp Nou at 9:45 a.m. Pacific Time, or 12:45 p.m. Eastern Time, on Matchday 1 of the UCL league phase.

After that match, Barcelona will not be back in action until Sunday, Sept. 13, when they visit Levante at the Ciutat de Valencia Stadium.

articles.title: Texas A&M stock report, from Saturday’s game against Missouri State
articles.summary: Texas A&M’s Week 1 Stock Report: After the big win over Missouri State, who’s rising, who’s slipping?
articles.body:
It was a rough first half for the Texas A&M football team, but whatever head coach Mike Elko told his players at halftime clearly worked. The Aggies responded with one of their most dominant stretches of football in nearly three decades, scoring 50 unanswered points while pitching a defensive shutout.

As mentioned above, the first two quarters were far from pretty. Most of the issues stemmed from the offensive line, which struggled to communicate in pass protection and failed to open consistent running lanes. However, as the game progressed and the staff began tinkering with the lineup, the unit improved drastically. By the second half, the difference was night and day.

The team's most notable strength is its depth , especially at the skill positions. Wide receiver and running back are both three‑deep with elite talent, making it difficult to predict who will earn the majority of snaps once conference play begins. Defensively, the Aggies weren't even at full strength and still held the Bears under 70 yards while creating two turnovers.

There was little to complain about, but plenty to clean up, particularly penalties and overall focus, both of which contributed to the slow start. Week 2 will offer a better opportunity to evaluate how this team responds to a stronger opponent. For now, below are the players who shined and those who disappointed in Saturday night's win.

It wasn't a flawless performance, but there were plenty of encouraging signs from Reed. Despite the drops and protection issues that plagued the first half, he did enough to maintain control of the game and, most importantly, avoided turnovers. Once the offensive line settled in and the rhythm improved, the offense opened up and Reed took full advantage.

In the second half, he looked completely comfortable, distributing the ball across the field and operating with the confidence you expect from a veteran starter. The Aggies blew the game wide open, allowing Reed to exit early as Hart took over once the outcome was well in hand.

Stats: 21 for 30 / 233 yards / 7.8 average / 2 touchdowns / 0 interceptions / 141.21 rating

The defense did exactly what you expected dominate from start to finish. The unit allowed just 67 total yards and held the Bears to 1-for-10 on third down, smothering every attempt to build momentum. While the pass rush wasn't as disruptive as it could be, producing only one sack, the Aggies still generated six tackles for loss and forced two fumbles, consistently collapsing plays before they could develop.

Bussey arrived at Texas A&M with plenty of fanfare and even chose to stay after Jimbo Fisher was fired, but his career to this point has been relatively quiet as he's continued learning the wide receiver position. Saturday felt like a meaningful step forward and a reminder of just how versatile he can be.

He finished with 55 yards on six touches and scored a touchdown, delivering one of his most productive outings as an Aggie. Considering the heavy rotation of substitutions in the second half, his impact stood out even more. Performances like this suggest he's beginning to settle into his role and could carve out a bigger share of the offense as the season progresses.

The graduate transfer jumped off the screen multiple times Saturday night. His biggest moment came late in the second quarter, when he delivered a crucial fourth‑down stop that completely halted the Bears' momentum. Later, he showcased his pass‑rushing ability with a perfectly timed strip sack, adding another game‑changing play to his résumé.

Henderson is yet another example of the depth this roster boasts and the kind of rotational impact the Aggies will need as the season continues.

It simply wasn't a clean game for the offensive line. There were too many penalties and too many breakdowns in both pass protection and run blocking. With four new starters and Holmon Wiggins calling plays for the first time, a learning curve was expected but the miscues in the first half were still costly.

The second half was much better, and the unit looked noticeably more cohesive once the staff began adjusting personnel. It will likely take a few weeks to find the right combination up front, but with such a thin margin for error in SEC play, they need to figure it out quickly.

Hart never quite found his rhythm after his touchdown toss to Aaron Gregory. He didn't make any glaring mistakes, but the number of open receivers he missed was concerning. The arm talent is obvious, and he made quick decisions both encouraging signs for a young quarterback, but his accuracy issues left plenty to be desired. That inconsistency is ultimately why he lands on the Stock Down list this week.

Stats: 4 for 8 / 36 yards / 4.5 average / 1 touchdown / 0 interceptions

articles.title: Ranking the Premier League’s best front threes: Man Utd fifth and Chelsea denied top spot
articles.summary: Premier League teams reshuffled their attacking options over the summer, but which side has the best front three?Liverpool, Chelsea, Arsenal and Manchester C...
articles.body:
Premier League teams reshuffled their attacking options over the summer, but which side has the best front three?

Liverpool , Chelsea , Arsenal and Manchester City all added fresh options this summer, with some signed for astronomical fees as the 20 Premier League clubs spent a combined £3.5bn.

We've ranked the best front threes in the Premier League right now.

5. Manchester United - Matheus Cunha, Benjamin Sesko, Bryan Mbeumo

Manchester United overhauled their frontline during the 2025 summer transfer window, as Matheus Cunha , Benjamin Sesko and Bryan Mbeumo all arrived in the same window.

The trio all reached 10+ goals in the Premier League as Manchester United secured a top-four finish and Champions League qualification. Each guarantees reliable returns, but do not quite fit into an elite bracket as things stand.

4. Arsenal - Christos Tzolis, Kai Havertz, Bukayo Saka

Arsenal signed Viktor Gyokeres as the missing piece of the puzzle last summer, and the Swedish striker scored 21 goals in all competitions last season.

However, Mikel Arteta has reverted to Kai Havertz as first-choice forward, valuing the German's all-round game. Arsenal had hoped to sign a marquee forward to fit alongside Havertz and Bukayo Saka this summer, though that role will instead be occupied by Christos Tzolis .

The Greek international recorded 59 goals and assists for Club Brugge last season, but the Premier League is a big step up.

3. Chelsea - Morgan Rogers, Joao Pedro, Cole Palmer

Chelsea's new-look frontline has started the season in style, with seven goals scored across wins against Fulham and Brighton.

Joao Pedro scored 23 goals during an impressive debut campaign at Stamford Bridge, while Cole Palmer has become a Premier League poster boy in West London. Palmer's sharp start to the season has been welcomed, alongside close friend and record signing Morgan Rogers .

Xabi Alonso's system gives real freedom to Rogers and Palmer in the pockets, a scary scenario for opposition sides.

2. Liverpool - Bradley Barcola, Alexander Isak, Cody Gakpo

Andoni Iraola will be rubbing his hands together after Liverpool's forward showed signs of clicking into gear on Friday night.

Cody Gakpo has started the season like a player with a point to prove after almost leaving for Manchester City, with the Dutchman recording two wonderful assists for Alexander Isak at Ipswich.

Isak has hit three goals in three league games, already matching his return from a tough first season at Anfield. The Swede scored 54 goals in 86 league games for Newcastle to cement a reputation as one of the league's leading number nines. If he can get back to that form, Liverpool have a real game-changer.

Bradley Barcola , a back-to-back Champions League winner with PSG, has arrived in a big-money deal to add further firepower.

1. Manchester City - Rayan Cherki, Erling Haaland, Antoine Semenyo

Manchester City top our rankings of the best Premier League frontlines. City's case is helped by the irrepressible Erling Haaland , whose mind-boggling goal record shows no sign of slowing down.

Haaland is the fastest footballer in Premier League history to have reached 50 and 100 goals in the division, and has now notched 115 in 135 games for the Cityzens.

Rayan Cherki 's twinkle-toed football has been a delight to watch, though it's style with substance, averaging a Premier League goal or assist every 98 minutes.

articles.title: 'In my blood': the Wales stars giving back to clubs
articles.summary: Modern sport can leave home a long way behind, but Welsh rugby is different, with many elite players remaining deeply connected to their roots.
articles.body:
Elite football tends to pull its best young players away early, away from their homes, their families and everything they know.

Lionel Messi was just 13 when he left Rosario for Barcelona, while Cristiano Ronaldo was a year younger when he traded Madeira for Lisbon.

And while football's pull rarely lets go, Welsh rugby is different.

There are past and present professionals across the country who remain deeply rooted in their community clubs.

Josh Adams has won 70 caps for Wales and toured with the British and Irish Lions, yet has still taken on the role of assistant attack coach at his boyhood club Hendy.

Wales back-row Aaron Wainwright is another example. He may have left Dragons for Leicester Tigers, but remains director of rugby for Whiteheads RFC.

Other players include Wales centre Joe Hawkins who helps out at Ystalyfera, Wales back-row Harri Deaves who is heavily involved at Pontyclun, while former Wales Under-20s captain Ryan Woodman gives time to Caldicot.

And before all of them, Wales and Lions forward Justin Tipuric was a shining example of giving something back having spent years coaching at Trebanos.

It is not just about coaching, it is what coaching represents.

These are not retired players easing into the next phase, some are still in their early 20s trying to establish themselves.

They are doing it while their own careers are happening, while the meetings, reviews, travel and pressure of professional rugby are still very real. Not afterwards but now, and not for the optics either.

This is not some tidy little side hustle, it is not a story for Instagram. Most of them probably do not even want the attention. It is just a way of staying connected - to the village, to the club, to the mates still there, to the game before it became a job.

Hawkins, 23, is one of the clearest examples.

"Ystalyfera is in my blood," said the Scarlets player.

"My grandfather used to be chairman and president at the club, my grandmother used to work in the burger van, my mother's been physio, my head coach now - Gareth James - is my cousin."

That does not sound like networking, it sounds like home, and when Hawkins explains why he does it, the point sharpens further.

"No, not at all," he said when asked if he is doing it for money or some kind of professional development.

"In the professional game, there's so much pressure at times to perform and everything. It's nice to come back to community rugby where everyone's doing it for the love of the game and just enjoying themselves."

That is the bit modern sport does not always leave much room for.

At the 2022 World Cup, only Qatar and Saudi Arabia had squads made up entirely of players from their own domestic league.

By the time many footballers reach that level, they have long since been absorbed into academy systems, agents, transfers and a career path that can leave home a long way behind.

Welsh rugby, for all its flaws, still leaves room for a player to go back and run a village session on a Thursday night.

"This is where it all starts for everyone and there are people who go on to play professionally. They all start in community rugby somewhere."

There is a bigger point here for Welsh rugby too. For a sport that spends much of its time talking about pathways, identity and reconnecting the professional and community game, it already has some of that connection in plain sight.

That is why Adams at Hendy is more than a nice local story.

It is a reminder that, in one important way, Welsh rugby still works differently.

Its players do not always disappear into the distance. Some still come back. Some still coach. Some still feel that the place which made them deserves something back.

And in a sporting age that keeps dragging its stars further and further from home, that feels rare enough to be worth holding on to.
